source_text: Quot igitur patrocinia naturae, quot privilegia gratiae, quot solemnia disciplinae, figurae, praestructiones, precationes religionem aquae ordinaverunt? Primo quidem, cum populus de Aegypto libere expeditus, vim regis Aegypti, per aquam transgressus, evadit, ipsum regem cum totis copiis aqua exstinxit. Quae figura manifestior in Baptimi sacramento? Liberantur de saeculo nationes per aquam scilicet, et diabolum, dominatorem pristinum, in aqua oppressum derelinquunt. Item aqua de amaritudinis vitio in suum commodum suavitatis Mosei ligno remediatur. Lignum illud erat Christus, venenatae et amarae retro naturae venas insaluberrimas, aquas Baptismi, scilicet, ex sese remedians. Haec est aqua, quae de comite petra populo defluebat. Si enim petra Christus, sine dubio aqua in Christo Baptismum videmus benedici. Quanta aquae gratia penes Deum et Christum ejus est ad Baptismi confirmationem. Nunquam sine aqua Christus, siquidem et ipse aqua tinguitur. Prima rudimenta potestatis suae, vocatus ad nuptias, aqua auspicatur. Cum sermonem facit, sitientes ad aquam suam invitat sempiternam. Cum de agape docet, aquae calicem, fratri oblatum, inter opera dilectionis probat. Apud puteum vires resumit; super aquam incedit libenter, transfretat; aquam discentibus ministrat; perseverat testimonium Baptismi usque ad passionem; cum deditur in crucem, aqua intervenit, sciunt Pilati manus; cum vulneratur, aqua de latere prorumpit, scit lancea militis.
pass_a_gloss: How many defenses of nature, how many privileges of grace, how many solemnities of discipline, figures, pre-instructions, prayers have ordained the religion of water? First, indeed, when the people, having been freely led out of Egypt, having crossed through the water, escaped the force of the king of Egypt, the water destroyed the king himself with all his forces. What figure is more manifest in the sacrament of Baptism? Nations are freed from the world through water, and they leave behind the devil, the former ruler, oppressed in the water. Also, the water is remedied from the fault of bitterness by the wood of Moses for its own benefit of sweetness. That wood was Christ, remedying the most unhealthy veins of a poisonous and bitter nature with the waters of Baptism, of course, from himself. This is the water that flowed from the rock, the companion of the people. For if the rock is Christ, without a doubt, we see the water in Christ blessed for Baptism. How great is the grace of water with God and His Christ for the confirmation of Baptism. Never without water is Christ, since He Himself is also baptized with water. The first rudiments of His power, called to a wedding, are inaugurated with water. When He speaks, He invites the thirsty to His eternal water. When He teaches about love, He approves the cup of water, offered to His brother, among the works of love. At the well, He resumes His strength; He walks upon the water gladly, crosses over; He serves water to those learning; He persists in the testimony of Baptism up to His passion; when He is given over to the cross, water intervenes, as Pilate's hands know; when He is wounded, water bursts forth from His side, as the soldier's lance knows.

bible_refs.note: water burst forth from His side

pass_b_english: How many natural defenses, how many gracious privileges, how many ritual solemnities, how many figures, prefigurings, and prayers have established the sacrality of water? First, when the people marched out of Egypt and crossed the sea, the water let them escape Pharaoh's power, then turned and drowned him with his entire army (Exodus 14:28). What figure could more clearly prefigure the sacrament of Baptism? Nations are freed from the world through water, leaving the devil, their former master, crushed beneath the waves. Again, when bitterness poisoned the water, Moses' wood healed it, restoring sweetness (Exodus 15:25). That wood was Christ, who from himself cures the toxic, bitter veins of our fallen nature with the waters of Baptism. This is the water that flowed from the rock that accompanied the people (Exodus 17:6). If the rock is Christ, then beyond doubt the water in Christ is blessed for Baptism. How vast is water's grace before God and his Christ for confirming Baptism! Christ is never without water, since he himself was baptized. He inaugurated the first display of his power at a wedding by turning water into wine (John 2:1-11). When he speaks, he invites the thirsty to his eternal water (John 4:14). When he teaches on love, he counts a cup of water offered to a brother among the works of love. At the well he regains his strength; he walks gladly on the water, crosses it, serves water to his disciples. He maintains the testimony of Baptism all the way to his passion. When he is handed over to the cross, water intervenes — Pilate's hands know it. When he is pierced, water bursts from his side — the soldier's lance knows it (John 19:34).

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both accurately reflect the Latin text. Pass B provides helpful scripture citations for the allusions (Exodus 14:28, 15:25, 17:6, John 2:1-11, 4:14, 19:34) which were not present in the Latin but are required by the instructions for identifying allusions. Pass A is a faithful literal translation. Pass B is a faithful fluent translation. All clauses, including the specific details of Christ's life (wedding, well, walking on water, passion, crucifixion), are preserved.
